item.title: 🗓 September 30 marks Victory and Independence Day, the Republic of Abkhazia’s main national holiday.

The Victory secured the right of the people of Abkhazia to self-determination and laid a robust foundation for the Republic’s sovereignty . #Victory81
8️⃣
5️⃣
years ago, on
30 September 1941
, the
#BattleOfMoscow
commenced — the largest defensive operation carried out by the Red Army during the initial stage of the
#GreatPatrioticWar
to
defend the capital of our Motherland
against the Nazi invaders.
The Nazi troops, which sought to seize the city within the shortest possible timeframe, were completely destroyed by the Red Army.
One of the key battles of
#WW2
ended in a
major and decisive victory for our people.
Despite their considerable superiority in manpower and military hardware, the
Nazi invaders suffered a crushing defeat
, which played a major role in paving the way for the eventual collapse of the Third Reich.
❗️
It was precisely near Moscow that the myth of the invincibility of the Nazi war machine was shattered once and for all.
Hitler’s blitzkrieg strategy
, which had previously been successfully employed by the aggressor in the occupation of a number of European countries (Poland, Denmark, the Netherlands, France and Belgium),
completely failed on the Soviet soil.
***
By the end of September 1941, the Nazis had
occupied the entire Baltic region, Belarus
and
Moldova
, as well as large parts of
Soviet
Ukraine
; they had
sieged Leningrad
and reached the approaches to Moscow. Given the strategic and political importance of the Soviet capital,
Hitler committed a powerful force — 1.8 million Wehrmacht soldiers and officers
, 1,700 tanks and around 1,000 aircraft. The Nazi command planned to seize Moscow within the first three to four months and completely
destroy its population.
The situation on the Eastern Front in September 1941 was extremely difficult. Nazi troops attacked Red Army positions along several axes simultaneously. In just two days,
Guderian’s tank group advanced 80 kilometres
, breaking through the front and encircling a considerable number of Red Army units in the areas of Bryansk and Vyazma.
In these circumstances, a state of siege in Moscow and the surrounding areas was put in effect.
Preparations for urban combat were intensified throughout the city,
while key government and industrial facilities were mined. Ordinary residents of Moscow and cadets of military schools joined Red Army personnel in
defending the city
. For two weeks, Soviet troops held back around twenty Nazi divisions in fierce fighting, making it possible to strengthen the defensive line and bring reserve forces up to Moscow.
❗️
During
#WW2
, no other capital had yet put up such determined resistance to Nazism.
In early December, when the Wehrmacht’s forces had been exhausted, the
Red Army was able to launch a counter-offensive.
The formations of the Western, Kalinin and Southwestern Fronts routed the strike groups of the enemy’s Army Group Centre.
German hordes were pushed back 100–350 kilometres
from the capital, and the Moscow, Tula, Kalinin and Ryazan regions were completely liberated from the enemy.
It was near Moscow that Hitler suffered his first major defeat of the Second World War.
Around one million defenders of the capital of our Motherland were awarded the Medal “For the Defence of Moscow”, while 110 people were awarded the title of
#HeroOfTheSovietUnion
.
🎖
In May 1965, on the occasion of the 20th Anniversary of the Victory, Moscow was awarded the honorary title of
#HeroCity
.
#WeRemember
#OurVictory

item.title: 🇷🇺 “From Cairo to Cape”: Vladimir Shubin’s Memoirs Presented in Johannesburg On 29 September, the “
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇿🇦 “From Cairo to Cape”: Vladimir Shubin’s Memoirs Presented in Johannesburg On 29 September, the “ From Cairo to Cape” , newly released memoirs by renowned Russian Africanist Professor Vladimir Shubin, were presented at the Nelson Mandela Foundation in Johannesburg. The event brought together more than 160 guests , reflecting the strong interest in Professor Shubin’s work and in the history of Russia-Africa relations. Among the distinguished guests were former President of South Africa and former Deputy President of the African National Congress Kgalema Petrus Motlanthe , as well as former Ministers of International Relations Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma, Lindiwe Sisulu and Naledi Pandor . The audience also included veterans of the African National Congress who witnessed and participated in the historic events described in the book, members of the diplomatic corps, representatives of business, academia, education, and journalists. 📖 From Cairo to Cape is both a historical study and a deeply personal memoir. Drawing on his first-hand experience, Professor Shubin tells the story of the people and events that shaped Africa’s struggle for liberation and examines the role played by the Soviet Union in supporting national liberation movements. The choice of the Nelson Mandela Foundation as the venue was particularly symbolic, recalling South Africa’s long struggle for freedom and the importance of international solidarity in the fight against apartheid and colonialism. 🤝 The Embassy

“From Cairo to Cape”: Vladimir Shubin’s Memoirs Presented in Johannesburg
On 29 September, the “
From Cairo to Cape”
, newly released memoirs by renowned
Russian Africanist Professor Vladimir Shubin,
were presented at the Nelson Mandela Foundation in Johannesburg.
The event brought together
more than 160 guests
, reflecting the strong interest in Professor Shubin’s work and in the history of Russia-Africa relations.
Among the distinguished guests were former President of South Africa and former Deputy President of the African National Congress
Kgalema Petrus Motlanthe
, as well as former Ministers of International Relations
Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma, Lindiwe Sisulu and Naledi Pandor
.
The audience also included veterans of the African National Congress who witnessed and participated in the historic events described in the book, members of the diplomatic corps, representatives of business, academia, education, and journalists.
📖
From Cairo to Cape
is both a historical study and a deeply personal memoir.
Drawing on his first-hand experience, Professor Shubin tells the story of the people and events that shaped
Africa’s struggle for liberation and examines the role played by the Soviet Union in supporting national liberation movements.
The choice of the
Nelson Mandela Foundation
as the venue was particularly symbolic, recalling South Africa’s long struggle for freedom and the importance of international solidarity in the fight against apartheid and colonialism.
🤝
The Embassy sincerely thanks Professor Vladimir Shubin for this
important and personal contribution to preserving the historical memory of Africa’s liberation
and the development of Russia-Africa relations.
#RussiaWithAfrica
#OurCommonHistory

🎙
Vladimir Putin
held a meeting
with President of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats Milorad Dodik and Prime Minister of Republika Srpska Savo Minic
(Moscow, September 29, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
In 2026,
a high-level delegation from Republika Srpska
took part in
the celebrations held in Moscow to mark the 81st anniversary of Victory in the Great Patriotic War
. We are
very grateful
to you for your participation.
The partnership between Russia and Republika Srpska is based on
a time-tested friendship
. For many years throughout our history, Russia, the Russian people, and the Serbian people have maintained
special ties
.
We will, of course, continue our efforts to further develop our relations
. This includes political dialogue, cooperation within the UN framework, implementation of joint economic projects, and, naturally, our traditionally strong contacts in the cultural and humanitarian spheres.
Together, we strive to establish a more just world order
. As I have already mentioned, we consistently support Republika Srpska at multilateral platforms, including the UN Security Council.
🗳
The date of the general elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina is approaching
: they are to be held very soon, on October 4. Russian representatives will participate as
observers
of the voting process. We wish success to the ruling coalition you represent.
We trust that no external influence will alter the views of the majority of the population or prevent patriotic forces from securing a mandate
to continue pursuing a course that safeguards the inalienable rights and interests of Republika Srpska within Bosnia and Herzegovina and fosters constructive cooperation with Russia.
We realise the complexity of the situation.
You are aware of our position on the post-Yugoslavia settlement: since the collapse of Yugoslavia, a fairer attitude towards the Serbs – the Serbian people – has been both necessary and essential for ensuring stability. After all, discrediting even a single participant in this settlement process cannot lead to stability and peace in this challenging region.
🤝
I would like to reiterate that
we sincerely wish you success
.
***
We are well aware that the Serbs are not seeking any special status or exceptions to the rules for themselves
. On the contrary, you are committed to fulfilling all arrangements and previously concluded agreements.
You have mentioned
Dayton
. I repeat:
you are not asking for anything special for yourselves
, only that the decisions adopted at the international level are implemented.
❗️
We consider it unacceptable to impose an external will on the Serbs
, especially in violation of previously adopted international agreements.

item.title: ⚡️ #KievRegimeCrimes Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
item.description: #KievRegimeCrimes ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik : 💬 Over the past week , Kiev regime militants focused their attacks on medical personnel, emergency workers and volunteers. They repeatedly targeted medical teams in the Belgorod and Zaporozhye regions. These crimes resulted in the death of one medical worker and injuries to seven others. In the Zaporozhye Region, a terrorist attack on a civilian vehicle delivering humanitarian aid killed three volunteers from the Omsk Region and injured another. The highest numbers of civilian casualties over the past week were recorded in the Belgorod, Zaporozhye, Kursk and Kherson regions and the LPR . Kiev’s armed groups continued their criminal strategy of “energy terror” in the Belgorod, Zaporozhye, Kursk and Kherson regions, the LPR and DPR, and the Krasnodar Territory. Ukrainian strikes on electrical substations left communities in the Krasnoyaruzhsky and Grayvoronsky districts of the Belgorod Region without electricity. A drone strike also damaged a radiation monitoring station at the Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant . On September 21-27 , shelling by Ukrainian neo-Nazis resulted in 315 civilian casualties: 274 civilians were injured, including nine children, and 41 people were killed. Over the seven days , Ukrainian militants fired at least 8,033 munitions at civilian facilities on Russian territory.
